chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated that Forat ibn Ibrahim ibn Forat al-Kufi said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Zahir said: He narrated to us Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Abdi known as Ibn al-Qari said: He narrated to us Sahl ibn Abd al-Wahhab said: He narrated to us Abd al-Qudos from Suleiman ibn Mihran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) that he said:

When the servant intends a good deed, a good deed is recorded for him; when he performs it, ten good deeds are recorded for him. When he intends an evil deed, nothing is recorded against him; when he performs it, he is given nine hours. If he regrets it, seeks forgiveness, and repents, nothing is recorded against him. If he does not regret it and does not repent from it, one evil deed is recorded against him.
ai.seo_question: How many hours does a sinner have to repent before an evil deed is recorded?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Shia emphasis on divine mercy, where the 'nine hours' grace period allows for immediate repentance before the sin is fully recorded. It underscores the principle that intention alone suffices for good deeds, while evil deeds incur a temporary delay in punishment, offering a window for *tawbah* (repentance) to erase the fault entirely.
